findings.reason: The protected latest-position map retains every distinct value encountered and therefore uses O(n) space even when k is small. The candidate keeps exactly the preceding k-position window in a set, preserving expected O(n) time while reducing auxiliary space to O(min(n,k)).

The candidate checks membership before insertion and removes position i - k only after the current comparison, so a value exactly distance k remains eligible. For k = 0, each value is removed in its insertion iteration and distinct positions can never qualify.

The legal 8/64/256-value tiers use k = n and place the only qualifying duplicate last, forcing the full lookup path. The candidate passes at +0.07 relative exponent; a correct scan of up to k preceding positions passes every output and fails only scaling (+1.18 relative exponent; 72.24x largest runtime ratio). The measurement note now binds size to n explicitly.
